drivingQuestion: May one recite Shema while walking through filthy alleyways with his hand over his mouth, and what becomes of one who stops or fails to stop?
outcomeNote: Both Rav Huna's permission and Rav Ḥisda's prohibition receive tannaitic support; the sugya rules for neither and turns to the fate of one who stopped or did not

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה יָשֵׁן בְּטַלִּיתוֹ, וְאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ מִפְּנֵי הַצִּנָּה — חוֹצֵץ בְּטַלִּיתוֹ עַל צַוָּארוֹ, וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: עַל לִבּוֹ.
segments.en: «The Sages taught:» One who «was sleeping» unclothed, but was covered «with his garment, and he is unable to stick his head out» from under the garment «because of the cold,» may «form a barrier with his garment at his neck and recite Shema» in bed. «And some say:» He must form a barrier with his garment «at his heart.»

segments.he: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא הֲרֵי לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה! קָסָבַר לִבּוֹ רוֹאֶה אֶת הָעֶרְוָה — מוּתָּר.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And» according to «the first tanna,» shouldn’t he be prohibited from reciting Shema because «his heart sees» his «nakedness,» as there is no barrier between them? The Gemara responds: Indeed, the first tanna «holds that» when «one’s heart sees» his «nakedness, it is permitted» to recite Shema, and a barrier is only necessary to separate between his mouth and his nakedness.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְבוֹאוֹת הַמְטוּנָּפוֹת — מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל פִּיו וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: הָאֱלֹהִים! אִם אַמְרָהּ לִי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּפוּמֵּיהּ — לָא צָיֵיתְנָא לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Rav Huna said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One who was walking in alleyways filthy» with human excrement and he must recite Shema, «he places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema. Rav Ḥisda said to him: By God!» Even «if Rabbi Yoḥanan had said it to me» directly, «with his own mouth, I would not have obeyed him.»

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְבוֹאוֹת הַמְטוּנָּפוֹת — מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל פִּיו וְקוֹרֵא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: הָאֱלֹהִים! אִם אַמְרָהּ לִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי בְּפוּמֵּיהּ — לָא צָיֵיתְנָא לֵיהּ.
segments.en: «Some say» this halakha: «Rabba bar bar Ḥana said» that «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One who was walking in alleyways filthy» with human excrement and he must recite Shema, «he places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema. Rav Ḥisda said to him: By God!» Even «if Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi had said it to me» directly, «with his own mouth, I would not have obeyed him.»

segments.he: וּמִי אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: תַּלְמִיד חָכָם אָסוּר לוֹ לַעֲמוֹד בִּמְקוֹם הַטִּנּוֹפֶת לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲמוֹד בְּלִי הִרְהוּר תּוֹרָה! לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן — בְּעוֹמֵד, כָּאן — בִּמְהַלֵּךְ.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges this: «Did Rav Huna» really «say that? Didn’t Rav Huna say: A Torah scholar is prohibited from standing in a place of filth, as he is unable to stand without contemplating Torah,» and uttering Shema orally is graver than mere contemplation. The Gemara responds: This «is not difficult; here,» Rav Huna prohibited contemplating Torah «in» a case where one is «standing» in a place of filth, while «here» he permitted to recite Shema «in» a case where one is «walking» through a place of filth.

segments.he: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּכָל מָקוֹם מוּתָּר לְהַרְהֵר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, חוּץ מִבֵּית הַמֶּרְחָץ וּמִבֵּית הַכִּסֵּא. וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכָא נָמֵי כָּאן בְּעוֹמֵד כָּאן בִּמְהַלֵּךְ — אִינִי, וְהָא רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה קָא אָזֵיל בָּתְרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וַהֲוָה קָא קָרֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. כִּי מְטָא בִּמְבוֹאוֹת הַמְטוּנָּפוֹת אִשְׁתִּיק. אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְהֵיכָן אֶהְדַּר? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ — חֲזוֹר לָרֹאשׁ!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Did Rabbi Yoḥanan» really «say that? Didn’t Rabba bar bar Ḥana say» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One is permitted to contemplate matters of Torah everywhere, except the bathhouse and the bathroom?» Consequently, it is prohibited to even contemplate Torah in a place of filth. «And if you say: Here, too,» there is a distinction between the two cases, «here,» Rabbi Yoḥanan prohibited contemplating Torah «in» a case where one is «standing; here,» Rabbi Yoḥanan permitted to recite Shema «in» a case where one is «walking, is that so? Wasn’t Rabbi Abbahu walking after Rabbi Yoḥanan and reciting Shema,» and «when he reached a filthy alleyway he fell silent» and stopped reciting Shema. When they emerged, Rabbi Abbahu «said to Rabbi Yoḥanan: To where» in Shema «should I return» and resume reciting it? Rabbi Yoḥanan «said to him: If you delayed» continuing Shema for an interval «sufficient to complete the entire» Shema, «return to the beginning» and recite it from there. From the fact that Rabbi Yoḥanan did not admonish him for interrupting his recitation, apparently he, too, prohibits reciting Shema while walking through a filthy alleyway.

segments.he: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ: לְדִידִי לָא סְבִירָא לִי, לְדִידָךְ דִּסְבִירָא לָךְ, אִם שָׁהִיתָ כְּדֵי לִגְמוֹר אֶת כּוּלָּהּ חֲזוֹר לָרֹאשׁ.
segments.en: The Gemara responds: This is not a proof, as «he says to him as follows: I do not hold» that one must interrupt the recitation of Shema in this case, but «for you, who holds» that one must, «if you delayed» Shema for an interval «sufficient to complete the entire» Shema, «return to the beginning» and recite it from there.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא, תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא. תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא: הַמְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְבוֹאוֹת הַמְטוּנָּפוֹת — מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ עַל פִּיו וְיִקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. תַּנְיָא כְּוָתֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ בִּמְבוֹאוֹת הַמְטוּנָּפוֹת — לֹא יִקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁאִם הָיָה קוֹרֵא וּבָא — פּוֹסֵק.
segments.en: The Gemara cites tannaitic sources to corroborate both the lenient and the stringent opinions. «It is taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rav Huna, »and« it is taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rav Ḥisda. It is taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rav Huna: One who was walking in filthy alleyways places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema. It is taught» in a baraita «in accordance with» the opinion «of Rav Ḥisda: One who was walking in filthy alleyways may not recite Shema. Furthermore, if he was in the course of reciting» Shema when he reached a filthy alleyway, «he stops» his recitation at that point.

segments.he: לֹא פָּסַק — מַאי? אָמַר רַבִּי מְיָאשָׁה בַּר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר: ״וְגַם אֲנִי נָתַתִּי לָהֶם חֻקִּים לֹא טוֹבִים וּמִשְׁפָּטִים לֹא יִחְיוּ בָּהֶם״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: If «one did not stop, what» is his status? «Rabbi Meyasha, son of the son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, said: Of him the verse says: “Moreover, I gave them statutes that were not good and laws by which they could not live”» (Ezekiel 20:25), as in this case following these statutes and laws led to sin, not to mitzva.

segments.he: רַב אַסִּי אָמַר: ״הוֹי מוֹשְׁכֵי הֶעָוֹן בְּחַבְלֵי הַשָּׁוְא״. רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״כִּי דְבַר ה׳ בָּזָה״.
segments.en: «Rav Asi said» that this is derived from the verse: «“Woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity”» (Isaiah 5:18), meaning that this man brings sin upon himself for naught. «Rav Adda bar Ahava said» it is derived «from here: “For he has shown contempt for the word of the Lord”» (Numbers 15:31), meaning that uttering God’s word in a place of filth shows contempt for the Lord.

segments.he: וְאִם פָּסַק מַה שְּׂכָרוֹ? אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב אוֹמֵר: ״וּבַדָּבָר הַזֶּה תַּאֲרִיכוּ יָמִים״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «And if he stopped» his recitation, «what is his reward? Rabbi Abbahu said: Of him the verse says: “And it is through this matter that you will prolong your days”» (Deuteronomy 32:47), meaning that by being careful with one’s speech one merits longevity.

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן
moves.summary: Baraita: one under his garment who cannot put out his head makes a barrier at the neck and recites Shema
moves.about: baraita: one sleeping unclothed under his garment who cannot put his head out for the cold makes a barrier at his neck and recites Shema; some say at his heart

moves.cueHe: ויש אומרים: על לבו
moves.summary: Some say the barrier must be at the heart
moves.about: where the barrier must be made: at the neck, or at the heart

moves.cueHe: ותנא קמא הרי לבו רואה את הערוה
moves.summary: For the first tanna, the heart sees the nakedness
moves.about: according to the first tanna his heart sees his nakedness, which should bar recitation

moves.cueHe: קסבר לבו רואה את הערוה — מותר
moves.summary: The first tanna holds that the heart seeing the nakedness is permitted
moves.about: the first tanna holds that when the heart sees the nakedness recitation is permitted; the barrier is needed only between mouth and nakedness

moves.cueHe: אמר רב הונא אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Rav Huna in Rabbi Yoḥanan's name: one walking in filthy alleyways covers his mouth and recites Shema
moves.about: one walking through filthy alleyways places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב חסדא: האלהים! אם אמרה לי רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Rav Ḥisda swears he would not obey even Rabbi Yoḥanan himself on this
moves.about: whether one may recite Shema while walking through filthy alleyways with his hand over his mouth

moves.cueHe: איכא דאמרי: אמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי
moves.summary: Variant: the ruling is transmitted by Rabba bar bar Ḥana in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi's name
moves.about: the same ruling is alternatively attributed to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi via Rabba bar bar Ḥana, with Rav Ḥisda's oath directed at him

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה רב חסדא: האלהים! אם אמרה לי רבי יהושע בן לוי
moves.summary: In the variant, Rav Ḥisda swears he would not obey even Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
moves.about: whether one may recite Shema while walking through filthy alleyways with his hand over his mouth (variant version)

moves.cueHe: ומי אמר רב הונא הכי
moves.summary: Rav Huna elsewhere forbids a scholar to stand in filth lest he contemplate Torah
moves.about: Rav Huna permits reciting Shema in filthy alleys yet forbids a scholar even to stand in filth lest he contemplate Torah

moves.cueHe: לא קשיא, כאן — בעומד, כאן — במהלך
moves.summary: Standing is forbidden, walking through is permitted
moves.about: the prohibition concerns one standing in filth, the permission one walking through it

moves.cueHe: ומי אמר רבי יוחנן הכי
moves.summary: Rabbi Yoḥanan elsewhere bars contemplating Torah in the bathhouse and bathroom
moves.about: Rabbi Yoḥanan permits reciting Shema in filthy alleys yet bars even contemplating Torah in a filthy place

moves.cueHe: וכי תימא: הכא נמי כאן בעומד כאן במהלך
moves.summary: Perhaps here too distinguish standing from walking
moves.about: Rabbi Yoḥanan's teaching that Torah may be contemplated everywhere except the bathhouse and the bathroom

moves.cueHe: איני, והא רבי אבהו הוה קא אזיל בתריה דרבי יוחנן
moves.summary: Rabbi Abbahu fell silent in a filthy alley while walking behind Rabbi Yoḥanan, who did not fault him
moves.about: the standing/walking distinction cannot hold for Rabbi Yoḥanan, since he did not fault Rabbi Abbahu for falling silent while walking through filthy alleys

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה לרבי יוחנן: להיכן אהדר
moves.summary: Rabbi Abbahu asks where to resume
moves.about: to where in Shema he should return after his interruption

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אם שהית כדי לגמור את כולה
moves.summary: If the delay sufficed to finish all of Shema, return to the beginning
moves.about: if he delayed long enough to complete the whole Shema, he returns to the beginning

moves.cueHe: הכי קאמר ליה: לדידי לא סבירא לי
moves.summary: No proof: Rabbi Yoḥanan answered according to Rabbi Abbahu's view, not his own
moves.about: Rabbi Yoḥanan meant: I myself do not hold one must interrupt, but for you who do, return to the beginning if you delayed that long

moves.cueHe: תניא כותיה דרב הונא
moves.summary: A baraita supports Rav Huna
moves.about: baraita: one walking in filthy alleyways places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema

moves.cueHe: תניא כותיה דרב חסדא
moves.summary: A baraita supports Rav Ḥisda: he does not recite, and if reciting he stops
moves.about: baraita: one walking in filthy alleyways may not recite Shema, and if already reciting he stops

moves.cueHe: לא פסק — מאי?
moves.summary: What of one who did not stop?
moves.about: what is the status of one who did not stop reciting in the filthy alleyway

moves.actor: ר׳ מיאשה בר בריה דר׳ יהושע בן לוי
moves.cueHe: אמר רבי מיאשה בר בריה דרבי יהושע בן לוי
moves.summary: Ezekiel 20:25 applies to him
moves.about: of one who did not stop, the verse says God gave them statutes that were not good

moves.cueHe: רב אסי אמר
moves.summary: Isaiah 5:18 applies to him
moves.about: of one who did not stop, the verse says woe to those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity

moves.cueHe: רב אדא בר אהבה אמר מהכא
moves.summary: Numbers 15:31 applies to him
moves.about: of one who did not stop, the verse says he has shown contempt for the word of the Lord

moves.cueHe: ואם פסק מה שכרו?
moves.summary: And what is the reward of one who stopped?
moves.about: what the reward is of one who stopped reciting in the filthy alleyway

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אבהו: עליו הכתוב אומר
moves.summary: Deuteronomy 32:47 promises him long life
moves.about: of one who stopped, the verse says through this matter you will prolong your days

edges.cueHe: איני, והא רבי אבהו הוה קא אזיל בתריה דרבי יוחנן
edges.about: the standing/walking distinction cannot hold for Rabbi Yoḥanan, since he did not fault Rabbi Abbahu for falling silent while walking through filthy alleys

edges.cueHe: והא רבי אבהו הוה קא אזיל בתריה דרבי יוחנן והוה קא קרי קריאת שמע
edges.about: Rabbi Abbahu, reciting Shema while walking behind Rabbi Yoḥanan, fell silent on reaching filthy alleyways

edges.cueHe: הוה קא אזיל בתריה דרבי יוחנן
edges.about: Rabbi Abbahu was walking behind Rabbi Yoḥanan as his attendant

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה לרבי יוחנן: להיכן אהדר
edges.about: to where in Shema he should return after his interruption

edges.cueHe: אמר ליה: אם שהית כדי לגמור את כולה — חזור לראש
edges.about: if he delayed long enough to complete the whole Shema, he returns to the beginning

edges.cueHe: הכי קאמר ליה
edges.about: Rabbi Yoḥanan meant: I myself do not hold one must interrupt, but for you who do, return to the beginning if you delayed that long

edges.cueHe: לדידך דסבירא לך
edges.about: Rabbi Abbahu holds that one must interrupt Shema in a filthy alleyway

edges.cueHe: תניא כותיה דרב הונא: המהלך במבואות המטונפות
edges.about: baraita: one walking in filthy alleyways places his hand over his mouth and recites Shema

edges.cueHe: תניא כותיה דרב הונא
edges.about: a baraita supports Rav Huna's permission to recite Shema in filthy alleys with hand over mouth

edges.cueHe: תניא כותיה דרב חסדא: היה מהלך במבואות המטונפות
edges.about: baraita: one walking in filthy alleyways may not recite Shema, and if already reciting he stops

edges.cueHe: תניא כותיה דרב חסדא
edges.about: a baraita supports Rav Ḥisda's prohibition of reciting Shema in filthy alleys

edges.cueHe: לא פסק — מאי?
edges.about: what is the status of one who did not stop reciting in the filthy alleyway
